name: Medieval Climate Anomaly intensifies
summary: Northern Hemisphere proxy records (tree rings, ice cores, marine sediments) document a sustained warm phase, ~0.3–0.6 °C above the 1961–1990 mean, between roughly 950 and 1250 CE. The North Atlantic warming opens the route to Iceland (874), Greenland (986), and Vinland (c. 1000); Europe-wide growing seasons lengthen.

_quarry.structural_significance: Climatic enabler of the 11th–13th century European demographic, agricultural, and territorial expansion; the warm phase ends in the early 14th century with the cooling that precedes the Great Famine.
